key_fields.colony_diameter: several mm to tens of cm

narrative.morphology: This filamentous cyanobacterium (Plate 1) forms macroscopic benthic mats covering stones and fine sediments in the shallow waters, of up to ~1 m depth (Plate 2, 3). At a later life stage pieces of the mat float to form floating aggregates (Plate 4). Microscopic examination shows free, straight, isopolar, unbranched filaments with a blue-green coloration and no mucilaginous sheath (Plate 1). Filament lengths ranged from 35 to 410 µm, with a mean length of 170 µm. The terminal cell was rounded, without a calyptra (cap-like structure), and the filaments occasionally exhibited granulation. Cells along the filaments were uniform in appearance, wider than long, with mean dimensions of ~ 12 µm diameter and 5 µm long. No cellular differentiation was observed, a characteristic feature of the order Oscillatoriales. Gliding ability is typical. Based on these characteristics, the cyanobacterium was initially classified as Phormidium sp., but molecular tools confirmed it belonged to the genus Koinonema, and is most likely a new species, to be named Koinonema galileica Kaplan-Levy et al.
narrative.ecology: Individual (microscopic) filaments of Koinonema sp. (Plate 1) attach onto new substrates and begin growing, accruing biomass and developing into macroscopic mats that cover extensive areas (Plates 2, 3). Later, air bubbles resulting from extensive photosynthesis cause peeling off and detachment of clumps from the mat, those float and aggregate at the surface (Plate 4), then die off, or settle on a new substrate to start a new accrual cycle - as detailed by Wood et al. 2015.
